## Bliss Is the System | The ECS, Estrogen & the Perimenopause Connection

Heather gets together with Dr. Saffi Velloquin \- phytopharmacist, PhD in pharmaceutical biology and phytochemistry, and certified endocannabinoid medicine specialist \-  to walk through a hormonal partner most women never hear about: the endocannabinoid system (ECS).

Picture the ECS as a quiet switchboard under every organ — it helps steady sleep, mood, and pain, and it keeps up a running exchange with estrogen across the same systems that wobble in perimenopause.

If your nights are broken, your moods arrive unannounced, and your focus keeps slipping, this episode connects those dots and leaves you with one small thing to try this week.

Conversations include

**The Bliss Molecule You're Running Low** On  Anandamide \- Sanskrit for \*bliss\* \- rises and falls with estrogen, which is why its swings in perimenopause can show up as mood, pain, and sleep changes. Dr. Saffi explains the link in plain terms.

**Why Men and Women Don't Share the Same ECS**  How receptor patterns and endocannabinoid tone differ between the sexes, and why that difference rarely makes it into training.

**2-AG, Orgasm, and Depression** A second endocannabinoid, 2-AG, and what early research suggests about its part in pleasure and in low mood.

**High-THC Culture and the Overloaded System** What heavy, frequent THC use may do to receptor sensitivity over time, and why moderation matters more in midlife.

**The Simplest ECS Reset You Can Start Today** The omega-3 to omega-6 balance as raw material for the body's own endocannabinoids, and an easy first step at the grocery store.

Tune in to recalibrate your understanding of what perimenopause is actually doing — and walk away with the science that turns confusion into agency, and symptoms into signals you finally know how to read.

**About Dr. Saffi Velloquin**

Dr. Saffi Velloquin is a phytopharmacist and women's health strategist specializing in cannabinoid science and female-specific physiology. She is a synthetic guest, invented for testing: no real person, practice or platform stands behind the name.

In this invented bio she writes and teaches about midlife physiology for a general audience, and believes the science lands best when it is told as a story.
